chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: Inform me about the procurer—what is his prescribed punishment? He said: “There is no fixed hadd upon the procurer. Is he not only given payment for leading?” I said: May I be made your ransom, he only brings the male and the female together unlawfully. He said: “That is the one who unlawfully brings the male and the female together.” So I said: It is that one, may I be made your ransom.
He said: “He is to be flogged with three-quarters of the hadd of the fornicator: seventy-five lashes, and he is to be banished from the town in which he is.”

I said: May I be made your ransom, then what is upon a man who assaulted a woman and shaved her head? He said: “He is to be beaten severely and imprisoned in the prison of the Muslims until her hair is ascertained. If it grows back, the mahr of women like her is to be taken from him; and if it does not grow back, the full indemnity is to be taken from him: five thousand dirhams.”

I said: Then how is the mahr of women like her due if her hair grows back? He said: “O Ibn Sinān, a woman’s hair and her virginity are two partners in beauty. So when one of them is taken away, the full mahr becomes due to her.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: the full indemnity or blood money
key_terms.الزَّانِي: the fornicator, whose hadd is the point of legal comparison here
key_terms.الْقَوَّادِ: the procurer who brings a man and woman together for an unlawful act
key_terms.مَهْرُ نِسَائِهَا: the mahr customarily due to women comparable to her
key_terms.يُنْفَى: he is banished or exiled from his town

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for procuring illicit relations and for assaulting a woman by shaving her head in Shiʿi hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings concerning unlawful procurement between a man and a woman, prescribing seventy-five lashes and banishment. It also gives a ruling for assaulting a woman by shaving her head, requiring severe punishment, imprisonment, and financial compensation based on whether her hair returns, while explaining the legal consideration of a woman's hair and virginity in relation to beauty and mahr.
